speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether he can provide an update on how the maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) sector of our aviation industry is currently coping with the present demands for their services arising from the increase in the past year of commercial flights in Changi Airport; and (b) whether the MRO sector will be ready to cope with the likely increase in flights in the coming months which may arise from the re-opening of China’s borders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: They are also investing in technology and innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, Pratt & Whitney announced plans last September to establish its Technology Accelerator here in Singapore, which will develop technologies to increase productivity and help the company meet future demand.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And if so, why efforts have been made to recruit them again?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is there any shortage of local MRO workers and professionals at this point in time?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think it is good now to paint a broader picture of the aerospace industry, and to welcome both new entrants to the aerospace industry and also workers who have left and can come back.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, we are attracting new MRO operations in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, there have been many MRO companies that have expanded their operations since last year.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They include Liebherr, who is expanding their in-house repair capabilities for hydraulic and heat transfer equipment.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They are also working with our EDB to train and develop programmes for their employees.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We also have Meggitt, who doubled the size of their centre of excellence to accommodate MRO capabilities for over 100 new aircraft components.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we are continuing to attract these aerospace companies into Singapore and helping them also to expand their offerings into Singapore and therefore increasing our manufacturing output.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Aerospace companies, as mentioned in my earlier reply, are actively recruiting talent to fill the various roles across all of the different MRO sub-segments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are many roles in demand, you might want to try including technicians, engineers, production associates; and companies are also keen to hire talented emerging areas such as digital services as well as autonomous technologies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This can enhance productivity and innovation in the MRO process.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we will focus on reskilling and upskilling workers in this regard.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are expanding the industry, we are also creating jobs and we also provide training.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I give you two quick examples, SkillsFuture Singapore transition programme on aircraft maintenance for technicians and then also there is a Workforce Singapore's career conversion programme.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it is not just bringing them in, providing jobs and skilling, but we are looking forward bound into the future.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), Rolls-Royce and Singapore Aero Engine Services Private Limited (SAESL) have set up the smart manufacturing joint lab to develop next-generation MRO and manufacturing capabilities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: More than 100 SMEs have thus far participated in the joint lab with some becoming qualified suppliers to global aerospace companies.
